method: Local TestClient, 166 shaped personas (+fixture personas), fake source-ingest owner with newest-first pages, 3000 evidence items, 0.2 s per owner request (slow) or unavailable after 0.2 s. 5 runs per cell. Harness: services/control-plane/bff/tests/test_quarterly_ranking_read_latency.py helpers.
root_cause: _pm12_public_quarter_evidence_refs called read_evidence_refs() with no page_size, so the port streamed every owner evidence page (EVIDENCE_OWNER_PAGE_SIZE=200) before filtering to the quarter. Cost grew linearly with total owner evidence; on hosted each owner request waits ~4 s.
fix: personas/service.py _pm12_read_all_evidence_pages: reads the COMPLETE owner evidence (page 500, the owner max) with no truncation and no ordering assumption, rows kept in owner page order. Page 1 gives total + offset token; remaining offset pages are fetched concurrently (<=8 workers, contextvars copied) so a slow-but-available owner is waited ~once per request (first page + one concurrent round) instead of once per page; total read time is capped by the evidence owner read timeout (over => surface unavailable, not silent truncation). Unavailable page => unavailable surface after one wait. Opaque tokens fall back to sequential complete follow. No cache/setting/endpoint/job; port unchanged.

profile_ms_before_after.method: 5 runs per cell, 166 personas, fake owner with 3000 evidence rows and 0.2 s per owner request; 'before' = page_size unset full stream (page 200, original behaviour).
profile_ms_before_after.reproduce: temporary pytest module (not committed) looping t._get(t._Owner(3000, unavailable, delay=0.2), route) with personas_service._PM12_QUARTER_EVIDENCE_PAGE_SIZE=None for 'before'; cProfile of the same call for per-step times.
profile_ms_before_after.persona_league_tiers: p50 0.516 s / p95 0.724 s locally; it makes no evidence-owner call and is not changed by this task, so before == after.
profile_ms_before_after.dominant_cost_before: 15 sequential owner requests x 0.2 s = 3.0 s of ~3.9 s; after: owner wait ~0.4-0.7 s (2 rounds) plus ~0.5 s compute.

notes: Review fix 2: removed the 3-page cap and newest-first early stop (owner order is append order; they silently dropped linked in-quarter evidence). Parity tests now cover 501 linked in-quarter refs behind 1600 newer refs in owner append order on all 3 routes, compared to the full unpaged stream.

Acceptance 2 honest limit: the owner list endpoint has no time/quarter filter and caps pages at 500, so exact output requires ceil(total/500) owner requests; they grow with total evidence (3000 rows => 6) but run concurrently, so latency does not grow linearly and the wait is bounded by the owner read timeout. A request count independent of total needs an owner-side time filter (new endpoint, out of scope per acceptance 6).

Acceptance 4: slow-available owner wait is paid in ~2 rounds regardless of page count (test: 3000 rows, 0.2 s => elapsed < 0.6 s with 6 calls); unavailable owner pays one wait; total read over the owner timeout => unavailable.
Acceptance 5: ranking p50 1.27 s (<1.5 s) with a 0.2 s/request slow owner; recommendations p50 1.46 s, also <1.5 s here.

Review round 2 fixes: (a) every owner read incl. the first now runs under one overall deadline (evidence owner read timeout) and worker threads are abandoned via shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True) instead of joined, so elapsed is bounded on single-page, offset (>8 remaining pages) and opaque-token paths (test_deadline_is_enforced_on_every_path asserts elapsed < 0.25 s with a 0.1 s budget). (b) A page that is empty after tenant filtering but carries a next token is now followed (test_empty_filtered_page_with_next_token_is_followed). Offset fan-out only when the first token equals the page size; otherwise sequential complete follow with loop guard. (c) Parity bug found by the strengthened test: the unpaged port read returns rows sorted newest-first while paged reads keep append order; rows are now re-sorted with the port's shared evidence_ref_sort_key so order matches the legacy read. (d) Beyond-cap parity test now re-attaches linked_object_summary to the real port's rows (normalize_source_ingest_evidence_item drops it), asserts 501 linked quarter refs survive the quarter filter, 5 owner calls, and full body/snapshot/surface equality vs the legacy unpaged read on the ranking and recommendations routes.

Round 3 (AC2 per OPERATOR DECISION above): evidence reads go to the existing owner filtered to the quarter window; in-window requests = ceil(in_window/500) and out-of-window volume does not change the count (test_requests_equal_ceil_in_window_and_ignore_out_of_window_volume: in_window 50/500/501/1200 x out_of_window 0/1600/6000). No cap, truncation, endpoint, cache, setting or job added. Old owners that ignore the window are still paged fully (identical output).

Profile caveat: the p50/p95 and owner_requests cells in profile_ms_before_after were measured with a fake owner that does not apply the window (3000 rows all in scope, 6 requests); they were NOT re-measured for round 3. The PR-description claims 'one page, 15->1, 0.6s' were wrong and are withdrawn; the request-count contract is the ceil() test, not those numbers.

tests.added: test_quarterly_ranking_read_latency.py (21 tests): exact owner request counts per total (no truncation) on 3 routes; unavailable paid once; slow-available wait not per page; over-timeout => unavailable; owner order preserved for 3100 rows; 300-row parity; linked >500 evidence parity; 501 in-quarter rows behind 1600 newer owner-order rows parity on 3 routes.
tests.assertions_changed: test_rows_keep_owner_order_and_are_not_truncated renamed to test_rows_match_unpaged_read_order_and_are_not_truncated (new test in this task, not an existing one): owner append order was the wrong oracle; legacy order is newest-first.
tests.round3: test_requests_equal_ceil_in_window_and_ignore_out_of_window_volume (12 cases); stub-PG test adjusted to find the COUNT statement because an extra non-ISO-row query now precedes it (no assertion weakened).

owner_window_contract.change: Existing GET /api/source-ingest/evidence/items gains optional captured_from/captured_before (half-open [from,before), capture time = available_time then event_time, naive=UTC, unparsable/missing never match). total counts the matching population; response echoes `filters` only when applied; summary stays whole-tenant. Shared by InMemory/JSONL (repository.py) and Postgres (pg_store.py: SQL with strict ISO guard and bound instants, Python fallback with identical predicate if the cast fails).
owner_window_contract.bff: _pm12_read_all_evidence_pages passes the quarter window; request count = ceil(quarter population/500), independent of total evidence. Old owners ignore the window and are paged fully (truthful, identical output, quarter filter still applied downstream).
owner_window_contract.limits: Linked-ness is not filtered owner side; BFF filter unchanged. Request count grows with the quarter's own population by design (operator decision). Real-Postgres parity test was SKIPPED in this run: no test DSN was reachable and starting a Postgres container was not permitted in this session; it runs when SOURCE_INGEST_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN is reachable. The PG SQL shape and Python-fallback are covered by fake-connection tests only; independent reviewer must run the real-PG test.
owner_window_contract.counterexamples_tested: 1600 newer + 501 Q1 rows: 2 calls with window vs 5 on old owner, same output; other-tenant rows never leak; empty window = 1 call; owner failure stays 503/unavailable.
owner_window_contract.pg_timestamp_parity: pg_store window query: rows whose stored time the strict ISO SQL guard does not recognise (e.g. 20260215, 2026-02-15T00:00:00+0000) are listed by a small SQL query and judged in Python with the legacy _capture_datetime rule, then joined into the window by append_id, so PG matches InMemory/BFF semantics. test_real_postgres_matches_in_memory_window_semantics now passes the raw schema.table and includes compact-date, +0000 offset, standard and outside rows.

operator_decision_ac2_verbatim: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-11-14T00:42Z (operator chose this explicitly in the Human/Ops chatbox after 4 consecutive AC2 rejections): AC2 is clarified, not waived. AC2 is met when quarterly ranking, recommendations and drilldown read evidence through the existing owner filtered to the requested quarter window at the owner (no paging through other quarters' evidence and no full-history streaming) with an evidence-independent constant number of owner requests for out-of-window evidence; the number of requests MAY grow with the requested quarter's own matching evidence (page size of the existing owner read), because AC3 requires every quarter-linked evidence ref and an unchanged ranking snapshot id. Do NOT add caps or truncation, do NOT add a new endpoint/cache/setting/background job (AC6 unchanged). A test must prove out-of-window evidence volume does not change the request count and that in-window requests equal ceil(in_window/page_size). AC1 AC3 AC4 AC5 AC6 AC7 are unchanged. The other P1 findings below still MUST be fixed: Postgres timestamp parity (legacy formats such as 20260215 and 2026-02-15T00:00:00+0000) with real-PG regression coverage, and the real-PG parity test identifier bug; reconcile PR description and evidence with the actual code. Quote this decision verbatim in evidence.json and the handoff.
